title: Getting Started as a Founder in Strawberry
description: Practical ways to prepare for the day, keep company communication moving, research important decisions, and turn repeated founder work into useful company workflows.
introduction: Founders move between meetings, customers, hiring, investor updates, inboxes, and company decisions. Strawberry is most useful when it takes one piece of that work from scattered context to a result you can review.

Start with the pressure that matters now. Strawberry can learn through a few questions, relevant connected apps, or both. Once the first result is useful, keep the accepted sources, format, voice, and review points so the same work gets easier next time.

sections.title: Start with one result that matters this week
paragraphs: Do not begin by redesigning the company. Pick a result that would make the next week easier: prepare for an important day, find the next customers, make progress on a fundraise, fill a priority role, or remove a recurring piece of administrative work.

Keep discovery light. Strawberry can ask one short question at a time, check relevant approved context in connected apps, or combine both. Before doing substantial work, confirm the result, the important uncertainties, and a concise plan.

skills.context: Build and calibrate a reviewable shortlist of the next customers.
Turn the next fundraise into a clear story, target list, and practical process.

sections.title: Prepare for the day, then close the loop
paragraphs: When attention is the bottleneck, a concise morning brief is a strong first workflow. Strawberry can bring together urgent messages, work due today, and the meetings that need preparation, with links back to the useful source material.

Before an important call, it can turn calendar, company, person, and relationship context into a brief you can scan. Afterward, the transcript can become decisions, action items, owners, filed notes, and a grounded follow-up draft. Messages remain drafts until you approve them.

skills.context: Walk into today’s important calls with the context that matters.
Turn the reliable meeting record into decisions, actions, and reviewable follow-up.

sections.title: Keep company communication moving
paragraphs: An overloaded inbox is a useful place to calibrate Strawberry around your judgment. Define the categories that matter, let it learn your reply style from approved examples, and review a small batch before expanding the workflow.
Strawberry can surface what deserves attention and prepare replies in your voice. It should not send, delete, archive, unsubscribe, or make bulk changes without explicit approval.

skills.context: Triage the email, LinkedIn, or other communication queue that needs attention.

sections.title: Turn company context into decisions and clear artifacts
paragraphs: Investor updates, board materials, company reports, and market decisions often begin with information spread across dashboards, documents, Slack, meeting notes, and the web. Establish which metrics and milestones matter, where they live, who will read the result, and whether an accepted report or deck should set the structure.

For outside research, agree on the decision, scope, evidence standard, depth, and desired output. Keep source links and dates, separate facts from inference, and make uncertainty or conflicting evidence visible.

skills.context: Map a market before choosing a segment, entering a geography, or building an account universe.
Turn approved source material into a polished, on-brand presentation.
Research companies and turn the findings into a clear visual brief.

sections.title: Grow one accepted result into a company workflow
paragraphs: Review the first result and correct its assumptions, depth, format, tone, sources, and tool choices. If the process proves useful, preserve those accepted choices as a company-specific skill instead of starting from generic instructions next time.

When several people need the same inputs, ownership, destination, or review behavior, turn the individual workflow into a shared one. Verify one real handoff before scaling it. Add a routine only after the underlying process has worked a few times and the team wants it to recur.

Other useful directions include modelling a major decision, mining approved product telemetry for patterns, preparing a weekly KPI review, or assembling a diligence pack. Introduce them when they solve a real problem rather than presenting a long list all at once.

skills.context: Find people for a priority role when hiring becomes the next constraint.
Make a proven workflow reusable across the team with clear review points.
